newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bank ASLK to sell movie tickets in offices.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bank ASLK to sell movie tickets in offices.

text.p: Belgian bank ASLK-CGER, in an unusual move to make better use of its banking network, plans to sell film tickets and travel vouchers through vending machines in its branch offices.

"These machines will increase the return on investment of our sales outlets, and give us a competitive advantage by offering something other banks do not have," ASLK management committee member Jean-Pierre Cardinael told a news conference.

ASLK, a 49.9 percent unit of Belgian-Dutch financial group Fortis, will install the machines in 100 of its 1,000 branch offices by the end of 1998. The first 40 will be operational by the end of next month.
Although petrol stations selling snacks have become a commonplace, there are few examples of banks offering non- financial services through their extensive networks.

Cardinael said ASLK's initiative had been inspired by La Caixa -- Spain's largest savings bank and a partner of ASLK-parent Fortis -- which has operated some 800 similar vending machines in Barcelona in the past three years.

Excluding personnel costs, ASLK will invest 100 million francs ($2.8 million) in the vending machine network. The machines will be accessible seven days a week, from 0700 to 2300 local time, not only to ASLK customers but for anyone.
Luc D'Haese, director of ASLK unit Teles Services which operates the network, called the 700,000 franc ($20,000) machines "the Rolls Royce of vending machines".

Integrating a multi-media PC, a touch-screen, keyboard, web-browsing technology and a certified ticket printer, the machines will allow customers to find out which films are playing, get a short review and even see a trailer.
After payment with a debit card, the machine prints the tickets.
"These are real tickets which give access to the theatre, not vouchers which force you to stand in line somewhere else again," D'Haese said.

ASLK has made a three-year deal with Belgian multiplex cinema chain Kinepolis and is negotiating deals to offer concert and theatre tickets as well. It also wants to sell air travel through vouchers which can be exchanged for tickets at the airport.

Asked whether ASLK was not fighting a losing battle with similar services offered via the Internet, Cardinael said "to my knowledge Internet still does not allow you to print your own cinema or theatre ticket."
In order to lure more users to the machine -- and thus potential customers to its branch offices -- the machines will also show job offers, real estate sales advertisements and electronic shopping.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
